title: University of Rwanda Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2026–2027: 170 Fully Funded Undergraduate Scholarships for African Students
summary: Applications are open for the 5th Cohort of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda for the 2026–2027 academic year , offering 170 undergraduate scholarships to eligible African students, refugees, and displaced young people in Africa. The scholarship programme is being implemented by the University of Rwanda in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation under a 10-year Scholars Program running from 2021 to 2031. The initiative is designed to expand access to quality higher education for talented young people who have limited access to opportunities, with particular attention to groups including young women pursuing Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), young people with disabilities, refugees, and displaced youth. For the 2026–2027 academic year, the University of Rwanda is recruiting its fifth cohort of undergraduate Mastercard Foundation Scholars across selected programmes offered through several University of Rwanda colleges and campuses. The scholarship combines comprehensive financial support with academic, psychosocial, leadership, professional development, mentorship, community engagement, and career-development opportunities. Application deadline: October 12, 2026 at 23:59. About the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda is part of a 10-year initiative running from 2021 to 2031 . According to the official call, the programme is intended to expand access to quality higher education for 1,400 talented young Africans with limited access to opportunities . It places particular emphasis on women pursuing STEM disciplines, young people with disabilities, refugees, and displaced youth. The programme is designed to create impact at three interconnected levels: Individual level: supporting Scholars to succeed academically, develop leadership capacity, gain professional skills, and transition toward dignified employment. Institutional level: strengthening the University of Rwanda s capacity to provide inclusive and supportive educational pathways. Higher education ecosystem level: contributing to broader transformation within Rwanda s higher education system and beyond. The 2026–2027 call represents the recruitment of the programme s 5th cohort and provides an opportunity for eligible recent secondary-school graduates and other qualifying applicants to pursue undergraduate studies at the University of Rwanda. What the 2026–2027 Scholarship Offers The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is described by the University of Rwanda as a comprehensive scholarship . For successful candidates, the scholarship covers a broad range of academic and student-support needs. Full tuition fees The scholarship provides financial support for the scholar s university tuition fees for the approved undergraduate programme. This means successful scholars do not have to independently finance the tuition component of their studies covered by the scholarship. On-campus accommodation The scholarship provides fully paid on-campus accommodation . This is an important component of the financial package because accommodation costs can represent a substantial barrier to university access for students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Laptop Successful scholars receive a laptop as part of the scholarship support. The recruitment portal also encourages students to have access to a smartphone to support blended learning while waiting to receive the laptop provided through the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. Learning materials The scholarship includes support for learning materials , helping scholars meet academic requirements without having to shoulder all associated educational costs themselves. Annual return ticket allowance The scholarship includes an annual return ticket allowance . This forms part of the comprehensive financial-support package described in the official call. Monthly stipend Successful scholars receive a full-year monthly stipend as part of the scholarship package. This is intended to provide support for students basic needs during their studies. Psychosocial support The programme also provides psycho-social support services . This reflects the programme s broader approach to student success, which goes beyond academic performance to include the social and personal wellbeing of Scholars. Academic mentorship and tutoring Scholars receive continued academic support through: Academic mentorship Virtual learning Tutoring The objective is to help Scholars successfully navigate their university studies and maintain strong academic performance. Career development The programme provides career development services, including: Industrial mentorship Career guidance Professional development Enterprise development Other career-oriented activities These services are designed to help Scholars prepare for the transition from university into professional life. Industry internships The scholarship provides access to uniquely sourced industry internships for professional development. This can give Scholars opportunities to connect academic learning with practical workplace experience. Leadership and community engagement Scholars participate in regular group meetings focused on personal and professional development. They may also participate in: Leadership congresses Community service Mentoring Go-back Give-back activities Other initiatives designed to strengthen their capacity to contribute to their communities The programme expects Scholars to develop not only academically but also as leaders and community contributors. Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2026–2027: 170 Scholarships Available For the 2026–2027 academic year, the University of Rwanda has allocated 170 undergraduate scholarships across selected academic programmes. The scholarships are distributed across six campuses and several colleges and schools. The approved programmes cover fields including: Engineering Architecture Environmental planning Urban and regional planning Mathematics Physics Statistics Biochemistry Information technology Information systems Computer engineering Mining engineering Economics Business Accounting and finance Medicine Pharmacy Clinical psychology Dental therapy Anesthesia Nursing Midwifery Law Social work Creative and performing arts English and African languages Agriculture Food science and technology Horticulture Veterinary medicine Aquaculture and fisheries Animal production Education Special needs education Early childhood education The programme therefore provides opportunities across both STEM and non-STEM disciplines. School of Engineering The following programmes each have three scholarships: BSc (Hons) in Civil Engineering — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Electrical Power Engineering — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Electronics Telecommunication Engineering — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Transportation Engineering — 3 scholarships School of Architecture and Built Environment Bachelor of Architecture with Honours — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Environmental Planning Management — 2 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Urban and Regional Planning — 3 scholarships School of Science BSc (Hons) in Biochemistry — 2 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Applied Mathematics — 2 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Applied Physics — 2 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Statistics — 3 scholarships School of ICT BSc (Hons) in Computer Engineering — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Information Technology — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Information Systems — 3 scholarships School of Mining and Geology BSc (Hons) in Mining Engineering — 3 scholarships Together, these programmes account for the 41 scholarships allocated to Nyarugenge Campus . Scholarship Allocation at Huye Campus The Huye Campus has scholarships across three major colleges: College of Business and Economics — 8 scholarships College of Medicine and Health Sciences — 87 scholarships College of Arts and Social Studies — 8 scholarships This gives Huye Campus a combined allocation of 103 scholarships . College of Business and Economics Eight scholarships are available across the following programmes: BSc (Hons) in Economics — 2 scholarships BBA (Hons) in Transport Logistics Management — 2 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Business Information Technology — 2 scholarships BBA (Hons) in Accounting Finance — 2 scholarships College of Medicine and Health Sciences The College of Medicine and Health Sciences has 87 scholarships , making it the largest scholarship allocation among the listed colleges. The programmes include: Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery — 8 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Pharmacy — 4 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Clinical Psychology — 2 scholarships Bachelor in Dental Therapy — 16 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Anesthesia — 17 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Midwifery — 20 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Nursing — 20 scholarships College of Arts and Social Studies Eight scholarships are allocated as follows: BA (Hons) in Creative and Performing Arts — 2 scholarships BA (Hons) in English and African Languages — 2 scholarships Bachelor s Degree (Hons) of Law — 2 scholarships BSoc (Hons) in Social Work — 2 scholarships The detailed allocation table is contained in the official signed call for applications. Scholarship Allocation at Busogo Campus The Busogo Campus , through the College of Agriculture, Forestry and Food Sciences, has 9 scholarships . The approved programmes are: BSc (Hons) in Crop Production — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Food Science Technology — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Horticulture — 3 scholarships The programme provides an opportunity for students interested in agriculture, food systems, crop production, horticulture, and related areas to pursue undergraduate study with comprehensive scholarship support. Scholarship Allocation at Nyagatare Campus The Nyagatare Campus , through the College of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Sciences, has 9 scholarships . The approved programmes are: BSc (Hons) in Aquaculture Fisheries Management — 3 scholarships BSc (Hons) in Animal Production — 3 scholarships Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine — 3 scholarships These opportunities are particularly relevant to students interested in animal health, veterinary medicine, fisheries, aquaculture, and animal production. Scholarship Allocation at Rukara Campus The Rukara Campus , through the College of Education, has 8 scholarships . The programmes are: BEd (Hons) in Computer Science — 2 scholarships BEd (Hons) in Science, with Physics-Chemistry — 2 scholarships BEd (Hons) in Special Needs Education — 2 scholarships BEd (Hons) in Early Childhood Education — 2 scholarships These programmes create opportunities for applicants interested in teacher education, computer science education, science education, special needs education, and early childhood education. Summary of the 170 Scholarship Places The scholarship allocation can be summarized as follows: Campus College/Area Number of Scholarships Nyarugenge College of Science and Technology 41 Huye College of Business and Economics 8 Huye College of Medicine and Health Sciences 87 Huye College of Arts and Social Studies 8 Busogo College of Agriculture, Forestry and Food Sciences 9 Nyagatare College of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Sciences 9 Rukara College of Education 8 Total All approved programmes 170 The signed call confirms a total of 170 undergraduate scholarship places for the 2026–2027 academic year. Who Is Eligible for the Mastercard Foundation Scholarship? The scholarship opportunity is designed for African students from all races, colours, and descent who have limited access to opportunities . The official call identifies several categories of eligible applicants. Rwandan citizens Rwandan citizens can benefit from the national scholarship quota . Applicants who are Rwandan citizens must meet the other stated eligibility and academic requirements. Citizens of other African countries The scholarship is also open to citizens of any African country , subject to the stated eligibility requirements and admission into one of the approved programmes. This means the opportunity is not limited to applicants from Rwanda. Refugees in Africa Refugees are eligible to apply. Applicants applying under refugee status are expected to provide appropriate legal documentation confirming their status. The call specifies that refugee applicants should provide legal proof of their status from recognized bodies such as UNHCR or NCPD , respectively, or another duly recognized organization. Displaced youth in Africa The call also includes displaced youth in Africa among eligible applicants. This expands the opportunity beyond conventional nationality-based scholarship categories and reflects the programme s focus on young people facing barriers to higher education. Young people with disabilities Young people with disabilities are specifically among the groups the broader Mastercard Foundation programme seeks to support. Applicants applying under a disability category are expected to provide the required disability certificate. The programme therefore combines academic selection with an effort to expand access to higher education for students who face structural barriers. Academic Eligibility Requirements Applicants must be academically qualified for their chosen programme. They must also meet the University of Rwanda s admission requirements for the particular undergraduate programme they wish to study. The scholarship call emphasizes that applicants must have: Appropriate academic qualifications. Met the admission requirements for their selected University of Rwanda programme. Applied for admission to the University of Rwanda. Obtained a University of Rwanda reference number . Selected one of the programmes approved under the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. Applicants should therefore not treat the scholarship application as a substitute for the University s admission application. The two processes are connected, and applicants need to complete the required University of Rwanda admission process before final scholarship consideration. Age Requirements The standard age requirement is: Applicants must not be above 28 years of age at the time of application. The call provides an extended maximum age of 30 years for applicants who can provide certified proof of circumstances that have prolonged their educational pathway. The document gives examples including: Refugees Single mothers Members of child-headed families Other qualifying circumstances recognized under the programme Applicants relying on the extended age provision should therefore be prepared to provide appropriate evidence supporting their circumstances. Leadership and Community Engagement Requirement Academic performance alone is not the only consideration. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to leadership and provide evidence of community engagement, giving back, and/or participation in transformation initiatives . This can include experiences in which an applicant has contributed to their school, community, organization, or wider society. The programme is seeking Scholars who can eventually use their education and skills to contribute to positive change in their communities and Africa more broadly. Economic Disadvantage and Limited Access to Opportunities The online recruitment portal explains that scholarship applications are assessed using a standard weighting system based on three principal dimensions: Academic Talent — 30% Economic Disadvantage — 45% Leadership Potential — 25% This means economic disadvantage carries the largest weighting among the three stated assessment areas. Applicants should therefore accurately communicate their socioeconomic circumstances in the application rather than focusing exclusively on academic performance. The programme is specifically designed for talented young people who have limited access to opportunities . The signed call also describes the scholarship as an opportunity for African students who face such access limitations. Existing Scholarship Holders and Continuing Students Applicants must pay close attention to the programme s restrictions concerning other scholarships and existing university students. The official call states that selected applicants who hold another scholarship must be willing to discontinue the other scholarship . If a double scholarship is discovered, the Mastercard Foundation scholarship will be discontinued. The call also states that continuing students are not eligible . The opportunity is therefore primarily intended for applicants entering an approved undergraduate programme rather than students who are already continuing their undergraduate studies at the University of Rwanda. Foreign Academic Qualifications and Equivalence Applicants who obtained their academic qualifications outside Rwanda must pay attention to the equivalence requirement. The online recruitment platform states that applicants with foreign academic qualifications must obtain equivalence from: Rwanda s Higher Education Council (HEC) National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA) Applicants with foreign qualifications should therefore begin the equivalence process early rather than waiting until the final stages of scholarship selection. International Students and Visa Requirements The scholarship is open to eligible African applicants outside Rwanda, including citizens of other African countries and qualifying refugees or displaced youth. The recruitment portal provides information concerning entry and study visas. It states that citizens of all countries can obtain an entry visa on arrival at Kigali International Airport . International students must then apply for a study visa within 15 days of arrival . The portal states that international students applying for the study visa will require: A police clearance A valid passport Scholarship holders coming from outside Rwanda should therefore prepare their travel and immigration documentation carefully if selected. University of Rwanda Student Number A University of Rwanda student number/reference number is an important part of the scholarship application process. The recruitment portal requires applicants to enter their University of Rwanda student number to verify eligibility and create an account. The signed call also requires applicants to have generated a UR Reference Number and to have applied for admission to the University of Rwanda in one of the approved programmes. Applicants should therefore complete the necessary University admission process before attempting to finalize the scholarship application. Documents Required for the Online Application The current Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program recruitment portal identifies several documents that applicants should prepare before beginning the application. University of Rwanda student number All applicants must have their University of Rwanda student number available. Passport photograph All applicants must provide a digital passport photograph with a white background . Identification document Applicants must provide a scanned copy of one of the accepted identification documents, such as: National ID showing date of birth Passport Refugee ID Disability certificate Applicants applying under the disability category should prepare their disability certificate . Leadership certificates Applicants who have leadership certificates should upload them as supporting evidence. The live recruitment portal currently indicates that uploaded documents should be clear and can be submitted in PDF, JPG, or PNG format , with a stated maximum of 5 MB per file. However, the signed September 2026 call contains a more restrictive instruction for final application attachments, stating that required documents should be saved in PDF format with a size of less than 250 KB. Applicants should therefore check the live portal instructions carefully when uploading documents and ensure that every file meets the system s current requirements. Click Here to learn More How to Apply for the Mastercard Foundation Scholarship The application process is conducted online. Applicants should use the official University of Rwanda Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program recruitment platform: https://mcfsprecruitment.ur.ac.rw/ug-recruitment/ The online process has three broad stages. Step 1: Verify Eligibility and Create an Account Applicants first enter their University of Rwanda student number . The system uses this information to verify eligibility before allowing the applicant to create an account. Applicants can save their progress and return to the application before the deadline. Step 2: Complete the Application Form The online form requires applicants to provide information across several areas, including: Personal identification Educational background Family information Socioeconomic circumstances Leadership information Applicants should provide accurate information and ensure that all supporting documents are available before submitting. Step 3: Review, Submit and Track Before submission, applicants should carefully review every response and confirm that all required documents have been attached. The signed call states that an application will only be considered after submission and completion of all required steps. It also instructs applicants to ensure that all fields and attachments are completed before clicking the final submission button. Once submitted, the application fields are closed and cannot be repeated or edited, according to the official call. Click HERE to APPLY Do Not Submit an Incomplete Application The University of Rwanda recommends that applicants begin the process only when they have the necessary supporting documentation available. This is particularly important because the signed call states that applicants must upload the required supporting documents before final submission. Applicants should therefore prepare their: Student/reference number Identification document Passport photograph Academic information Disability certificate, where applicable Leadership certificates, where applicable Other required supporting documentation before completing the final submission. Scholarship Selection Process The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda uses a structured selection process. The programme explains that applicants are assessed according to established selection criteria, including: Academic qualification and talent Economic disadvantage Leadership potential Community engagement Eligibility requirements Admission to an approved programme The recruitment committee selects candidates based on the established criteria. Interviews Pre-selected applicants will be invited to participate in an oral interview . The official call states that interviews are conducted by independent panels . The interviews use a predefined interview guide aligned with the expectations of the programme and the vision of the University of Rwanda. Applicants are expected to receive equal treatment, particularly regarding interview questions. Home Visits The selection process may also involve on-site validation visits to the homes of selected students . This is part of the programme s verification process and may be used to validate information provided during the application and selection stages. Applicants should therefore ensure that information concerning their socioeconomic circumstances and other relevant aspects of their application is accurate. Verification and Disqualification The official call contains strict provisions concerning false information and attempts to influence the selection process. Applicants discovered to have: Falsified information Attempted to influence the scholarship process Provided misleading information during the application Attempted to improperly influence selection during an interview or home visit may be disqualified. The University of Rwanda therefore emphasizes accuracy, honesty, and transparency throughout the application process. No Fees, Agents or Intermediaries One of the most important warnings in the official call is that applicants do not need to pay charges, fees, facilitation payments, agent fees, or intermediary fees at any stage of the application process . The programme explicitly states that there are no charges, fees, facilitations, agents, or intermediaries required at any stage. Applicants should therefore be extremely cautious if anyone claims that payment is necessary to obtain the scholarship or influence the selection process. Keep Your Contact Information Active Applicants should provide telephone numbers and email addresses that remain active throughout the selection process. The University of Rwanda states that these contact details should be active at all times so applicants can receive important information about their applications. Applicants should therefore regularly monitor the email address and telephone number submitted in their application. The Application Is a Staged Process The University of Rwanda states that the scholarship application is a staggered ongoing process . Applicants should not assume that submission immediately results in selection. The process can include: Application Eligibility screening Shortlisting Interviews Verification Selection Publication of approved candidates Issuance of scholarship award letters Acceptance and confirmation Only candidates who successfully progress through the relevant stages will receive further communication. Publication of Selected Candidates The approved list of selected scholarship candidates will be published on the University of Rwanda website . Successful candidates will receive scholarship award letters. The official call states that award letters will be issued through the Office of the Vice Chancellor of the University of Rwanda . What Happens After Selection? Successful candidates will receive: A scholarship award letter A scholarship acceptance form The candidate must complete and sign the acceptance form to confirm acceptance of the scholarship. Parents or guardians of successful candidates are also required to complete and sign a commitment form confirming their support for the Scholar. Completed and signed forms must be returned through the programme email within five working days after receiving the scholarship award letter. If a selected candidate declines the scholarship for any reason, the call states that the next candidate in line based on performance will be awarded the scholarship. The call also states that a scholarship offer cannot be deferred. Expectations After Becoming a Mastercard Foundation Scholar The scholarship is not presented solely as a financial award. The programme expects successful Scholars to become: Transformative leaders Champions Entrepreneurs Change-makers Contributors to their communities Participants in initiatives that create positive change in Africa The programme expects Scholars to remain in close communication with the University of Rwanda for at least five years after completing their studies . This reflects the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program s broader objective of developing graduates who contribute to transformation beyond their university education. Academic Performance and Continued Scholarship Funding Scholarship support is subject to satisfactory academic performance. The official call states that scholarships will be reviewed on a rolling basis , meaning annual renewal of funding is subject to Scholars maintaining satisfactory academic performance. Being selected for the programme therefore does not mean that academic performance ceases to matter after admission. Scholars are expected to remain academically engaged and meet the University s academic requirements. Conduct and Disqualification The University of Rwanda also identifies conduct-related circumstances that can lead to automatic disqualification and loss of the scholarship. The call states that misconduct involving violations of University rules, regulations, and policies can result in loss of the scholarship. It specifically identifies conduct including: Participation in riotous acts Involvement in subversive activities Illicit financial activities Terrorism Denial of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi Propagation of genocidal ideology as grounds for automatic disqualification and loss of the scholarship where applicable. Academic Programmes Covered by the Scholarship The scholarship is not available for every undergraduate programme at the University of Rwanda. Applicants must choose from the specific programmes approved for the 2026–2027 Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program . The approved fields span STEM and non-STEM areas, including engineering, ICT, medicine, health sciences, agriculture, veterinary medicine, education, business, law, social sciences, and related fields. Applicants should therefore carefully compare their intended programme with the official scholarship programme list before submitting an application. Applying for a programme that is not included in the approved scholarship allocation does not establish eligibility for Mastercard Foundation funding. Why Applicants Should Apply for University Admission Early The scholarship application requires a University of Rwanda reference number and evidence that the applicant has applied for admission to an eligible programme. Applicants should therefore not wait until the scholarship deadline before beginning their University of Rwanda admission process. A practical approach is to: Review the approved scholarship programmes. Select a programme that matches your academic background and career interests. Review the University s admission requirements. Apply for admission. Obtain the required University of Rwanda reference number. Prepare scholarship supporting documents. Complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application. Submit before the scholarship deadline. Application Deadline The official deadline for the 5th Cohort Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda is: 12 October 2026 at 23:59. The live scholarship recruitment portal displays the same closing date and time: Applications close on 12 October 2026 at 23:59. Applicants should submit well before the final deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. Important Information for International African Applicants Applicants from other African countries should understand that admission to the University of Rwanda and scholarship selection are connected but distinct considerations. An applicant must: Qualify academically. Meet the University s admission requirements. Apply for an eligible undergraduate programme. Obtain the required UR reference number. Meet the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program eligibility criteria. Demonstrate the required leadership and community engagement. Meet the socioeconomic and other selection criteria. Complete the scholarship application correctly. International applicants who are eventually selected will also need to comply with Rwanda s immigration requirements. Support and Contact Information The official call provides several University of Rwanda contacts for applicants who require assistance during the application period. Official Application Portal Applications are submitted online through the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda undergraduate recruitment portal : https://mcfsprecruitment.ur.ac.rw/ug-recruitment/ Applicants can use the portal to: Verify their eligibility. Create an account. Complete the application. Upload supporting documents. Submit their application. Track application status through their dashboard. The University of Rwanda s main website also hosts the official scholarship announcement and signed call for applications: https://www.ur.ac.rw/ Frequently Asked Questions Is the University of Rwanda Mastercard Foundation scholarship fully funded? The official call describes it as a comprehensive scholarship covering full tuition fees, fully paid on-campus accommodation, a laptop, learning materials, annual return ticket allowance, and a full-year monthly stipend, alongside academic, psychosocial, career, mentorship, leadership, and professional-development support. How many scholarships are available? There are 170 undergraduate scholarships for the 2026–2027 academic year. Who can apply? The call is open to eligible African students, including Rwandan citizens, citizens of other African countries, refugees, and displaced youth in Africa, subject to the stated academic, age, socioeconomic, leadership, admission, and other requirements. Can students from outside Rwanda apply? Yes. The call specifically includes citizens of any African country, as well as qualifying refugees and displaced youth in Africa. Can refugees apply? Yes. Refugees are explicitly included among eligible applicants, provided they meet the other requirements and provide appropriate legal documentation of their status. Can applicants with disabilities apply? Yes. Young people with disabilities are among the groups targeted by the programme, and applicants in the disability category are required to provide a disability certificate. What is the maximum age? The standard maximum age is 28 years at the time of application . An upper limit of 30 years is permitted for applicants with certified proof of circumstances that prolonged their educational pathway, including examples such as refugee status, single motherhood, and child-headed family circumstances. Do I need to be admitted to the University of Rwanda? Applicants must have applied for admission to the University of Rwanda in one of the approved programmes and must have generated a University of Rwanda reference number. Can continuing University of Rwanda students apply? No. The official call states that continuing students are not eligible. Can I hold another scholarship at the same time? Conclusion The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda 2026–2027 provides a major opportunity for eligible African students who face limited access to higher education to pursue undergraduate studies with comprehensive financial and developmental support. The programme is particularly focused on talented African young people with limited access to opportunities and places significant emphasis on academic talent, economic disadvantage, and leadership potential . title: Microsoft Government Affairs Internship in Belgium 2026: Finance, Operations and Management Assistant Coordinator

title: FOR-GHP Fellowship 2027–2028: Fully Funded Outbreak Readiness Training for Public Health Professionals in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: The Fellowship in Outbreak Readiness for Global Health Protection (FOR-GHP) is inviting qualified public health and biomedical professionals from sub-Saharan Africa to apply for a comprehensive 1.5-year fellowship focused on outbreak preparedness, infectious disease response, One Health, global health security, leadership, and public health workforce development. Funded by the German Federal Ministry of Health through the Global Health Protection Programme (GHPP) , the FOR-GHP Fellowship is designed to strengthen the ability of public health professionals and institutions to prepare for, prevent, detect, and respond effectively to disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. The programme combines in-person workshops, online learning, self-study eLearning modules, case-study development, simulation-based learning, teaching activities, and regional networking . Fellows will be trained not only to strengthen their own professional competencies but also to become facilitators and multipliers who can transfer knowledge and skills to colleagues within their institutions and countries. There are no tuition fees , and the fellowship provides financial support for participation in the required workshops, including economy-class flights, visa fees, accommodation, and meals. The application deadline is 21 October 2026 at midnight CET . About the FOR-GHP Fellowship Programme The Fellowship in Outbreak Readiness for Global Health Protection (FOR-GHP) is an initiative funded by the German Federal Ministry of Health under the Global Health Protection Programme (GHPP) . The programme responds to the growing need for highly skilled professionals who can support effective outbreak preparedness and response. Natural disease outbreaks, emerging infectious diseases, and intentional biological threats can place significant pressure on public health systems. Strong preparedness therefore depends on having professionals with the technical knowledge, leadership skills, communication abilities, and institutional capacity required to respond effectively. FOR-GHP follows a multiplier approach . Rather than focusing only on individual professional development, the programme prepares fellows to transfer the knowledge and competencies they acquire to colleagues and institutions in their home countries. The fellowship is delivered through an experienced international consortium comprising: Africa Field Epidemiology Network (AFENET) Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine (BNITM) Robert Koch Institute (RKI) Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute (Swiss TPH) Through blended learning and practical training approaches, the programme seeks to empower local experts who can contribute to stronger public health systems and create wider regional impact. Why Outbreak Readiness Matters Disease outbreaks can emerge rapidly and spread across communities, countries, and continents. Effective outbreak management requires coordinated surveillance, timely data analysis, evidence-based decision-making, effective communication, trained personnel, and collaboration between different sectors. The programme recognises that public health emergencies cannot always be addressed by one institution or discipline alone. Consequently, FOR-GHP places particular emphasis on One Health , global health security, cross-sectoral collaboration, and systems thinking. The fellowship is intended to help strengthen the workforce responsible for implementing outbreak preparedness and response measures while supporting the obligations established under the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) . Objectives of the FOR-GHP Fellowship The fellowship has four major objectives. 1. Strengthen outbreak management competencies Fellows will develop competencies in outbreak preparedness and management, with particular emphasis on One Health and global health security . Training will use a combination of digital learning, face-to-face workshops, practical exercises, and simulations. The approach is designed to help participants understand both the technical and operational aspects of responding to public health emergencies. 2. Develop facilitators, multipliers and leaders The programme is not simply designed to train participants as individual practitioners. Fellows will also learn how to become facilitators, multipliers and leaders within their institutions and countries. This includes developing context-specific teaching case studies that can be used to share knowledge and strengthen the skills of other public health professionals. 3. Strengthen regional collaboration FOR-GHP seeks to facilitate capacity-strengthening activities within regional networks. Through collaboration and knowledge exchange, fellows will be able to build professional connections with colleagues working in different institutions and countries. This regional approach is intended to support: Knowledge sharing Professional collaboration Cross-border partnerships Coordinated outbreak preparedness Coordinated outbreak response Peer learning Public health capacity development 4. Promote long-term sustainability The programme will establish and nurture an active alumni network. The alumni network is intended to support continued collaboration, mentorship, peer learning, and professional engagement after fellows have completed the formal training programme. This creates an opportunity for the relationships and knowledge developed during the fellowship to continue producing benefits beyond the programme itself. What the FOR-GHP Fellowship Will Teach The fellowship focuses on a broad range of competencies related to outbreak preparedness, public health emergency response, training, leadership, communication, and workforce development. Participants will develop skills in the following areas. Collaborative Infectious Disease Surveillance Fellows will learn approaches for integrating infectious disease surveillance and public health intelligence. This includes working with data collected from multiple sources and understanding how information from different sectors can be harmonised, analysed, and interpreted. The programme particularly considers information across: Human health Animal health Environmental health This reflects the One Health approach, which recognises the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health. Public Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Participants will strengthen their ability to apply evidence-informed principles for preparing for and responding to public health emergencies. The training covers both unintentional and intentional public health emergencies and considers the obligations associated with the International Health Regulations (2005) . This competency is intended to help fellows contribute to stronger preparedness systems within their institutions and countries. Training and Adult Learning An important component of FOR-GHP is preparing participants to become trainers and multipliers. Fellows will learn how to: Co-create training initiatives Deliver professional training Evaluate training programmes Develop context-sensitive teaching materials Apply adult-learning principles Use case-based learning Use simulation approaches Support lifelong learning Participants will develop their own teaching case studies during the programme and subsequently use them in their home institutions. Public Health Communication Effective communication is essential during disease outbreaks and other emergencies. The fellowship will therefore strengthen participants ability to communicate public health evidence, outbreak information, and training content to different audiences. Fellows will learn to adapt their communication approaches according to: The target audience Cultural context Communication needs Level of urgency Nature of the public health information Transformational Leadership The programme also focuses on leadership in public health emergencies and learning environments. Fellows will be expected to demonstrate ethical, inclusive, and accountable leadership while learning how to inspire and empower others to work toward shared public health goals. Systems Thinking and Partnerships Outbreak preparedness frequently requires collaboration across institutions, sectors, and national borders. FOR-GHP therefore develops systems-thinking competencies that allow participants to engage with different stakeholders and build partnerships and coalitions. This is intended to support coordinated approaches to outbreak preparedness and response. Sustainable Public Health Workforce Development The fellowship also seeks to strengthen public health workforce capacity through: Communities of practice Peer learning Mentorship Professional networks Knowledge exchange Long-term collaboration These components are designed to ensure that learning continues beyond the formal fellowship period. FOR-GHP Fellowship Programme Structure The FOR-GHP programme runs for approximately 1.5 years and follows a blended Training-of-Trainers (ToT) model. The programme combines three major components: Three one-week in-person workshops Distance-based learning and case-study development between workshops Self-study eLearning modules The three in-person workshops will take place in Hamburg, Germany; Accra, Ghana; and Kampala, Uganda . Stage 1: Seven eLearning Modules The programme begins with seven eLearning modules. These modules will form an important part of the selection process because applicants will be assessed based partly on their performance in the online learning component. The eLearning period runs from: 1 December 2026 to 1 January 2027 Applicants should therefore be prepared to dedicate sufficient time to completing the modules and participating in the assessment process. Stage 2: First Workshop in Hamburg, Germany Successful participants will attend the first in-person workshop in Hamburg, Germany . The workshop is scheduled for: 12–17 April 2027 The first workshop will provide an opportunity for fellows to engage directly with trainers and other participants while developing competencies relevant to outbreak preparedness and response. Following the first workshop, participants will begin developing a teaching case study that will eventually be piloted as part of the programme. Stage 3: First In-Between Workshop Phase After the Hamburg workshop, fellows will enter a distance-based learning phase. During this period, participants will work on developing a case study that is ready for piloting. The case study is expected to be relevant to the fellow s professional and institutional context. This component is particularly important because the fellowship is designed around the multiplier concept. Participants are not only expected to learn but also to develop resources that can subsequently be used to train others. Stage 4: Second Workshop in Accra, Ghana The second in-person workshop will take place in Accra, Ghana . It is scheduled for: 11–15 October 2027 During this workshop, fellows will pilot-test their self-developed teaching case studies. The pilot-testing process provides an opportunity for participants to receive feedback, refine their training approaches, and strengthen the practical application of their learning. Stage 5: Implementation at the Home Institution After the second workshop, fellows will enter another distance-based learning and implementation phase. Participants will be expected to implement their teaching case studies at their home institutions. This step is central to the programme s multiplier approach because fellows will apply the knowledge and training resources developed during the fellowship to support capacity strengthening within their own institutions. Stage 6: Third Workshop in Kampala, Uganda The final in-person workshop will take place in Kampala, Uganda . It is scheduled for: 3–7 July 2028 Participants will take part in the Sustainability Strengthening Initiative (SSI) during this final workshop. The final stage focuses on sustaining the knowledge, networks, training capacity, and institutional impact developed throughout the fellowship. FOR-GHP Fellowship Completion and Certification Participants who successfully complete the programme will receive a FOR-GHP fellowship certificate . Successful fellows will also receive 10 European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS) points from the University of Basel for 300 hours of structured independent training and study. The certification and academic credit provide formal recognition of the learning and training completed during the programme. FOR-GHP Fellowship Eligibility Requirements The fellowship is primarily designed for professionals working in sub-Saharan Africa . Applicants should carefully review all eligibility requirements before applying. 1. Origin and Employment in Sub-Saharan Africa The programme is intended to strengthen public health structures across sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants should therefore have an origin from and employment in the sub-Saharan African region . The opportunity is consequently targeted at professionals who are connected to public health systems and institutions in the region. 2. Professional Experience Applicants must have at least two years of professional experience in either: Public health; or The biomedical sector. Experience related to the management, prevention, and control of infectious diseases is particularly preferred. Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate relevant professional experience rather than relying solely on academic qualifications. 3. Academic Background Applicants should have a degree or demonstrated proficiency in at least one relevant field. Eligible academic or professional disciplines include: Public Health Medicine Epidemiology Microbiology Biology Allied health sciences Applicants from related health-science backgrounds should carefully assess whether their education and professional experience align with the programme s focus. 4. Employer Endorsement Applicants must provide an endorsement document from their current employer . The endorsement should confirm that the applicant is permitted to participate in the fellowship alongside their employment. Importantly, the employer must confirm that the fellow will be: Released from work to attend all three in-person workshops Supported in completing the programme Supported in implementing the teaching case study at their institution Applicants should therefore discuss the fellowship with their employers before submitting an application. 5. Letter of Recommendation Applicants must provide a letter of recommendation from at least one current and contactable referee. The reference must: Be from a current reference Not be older than three years Include the referee s contact information Include an email address Include a telephone number Applicants should ensure that their referees are aware that they may be contacted during the selection process. 6. English Language Proficiency Advanced proficiency in English is essential because English will be used for course participation, learning, assessments, and interviews. The programme accepts several forms of evidence of English proficiency, including: TOEFL Paper: 550 TOEFL Computer: 213 TOEFL Internet: 79–80 IELTS: 6.0 Being a native English speaker Having completed higher education in English, provided written proof is supplied Applicants relying on higher education conducted in English should be prepared to provide appropriate written evidence. 7. Computer and Internet Requirements Because parts of the programme will be delivered virtually, participants must have access to: A computer A stable internet connection Functioning audio A functioning microphone Participation using only a mobile phone or tablet is not permitted . Applicants should therefore ensure that they have suitable equipment and reliable connectivity before applying. Participants may also be required to purchase additional airtime or internet data when necessary to participate in virtual activities. FOR-GHP Fellowship Selection Process Because the number of fellowship places is limited, applicants will go through a three-stage selection process . Stage One: Access to the Seven eLearning Modules The programme steering board will initially assess applications and select applicants who will be granted access to the first seven eLearning modules. This stage is scheduled for December 2026 . The eLearning modules will subsequently contribute to the assessment of applicants. Stage Two: Pre-Qualification and Interviews Applicants will be assessed based on their performance in the seven eLearning modules. The selection process will also consider: A pre-qualification test A short essay Additional selection criteria Selected applicants will then be invited to participate in individual selection interviews. The interviews will be conducted in English via Zoom and are scheduled to take place in January 2027 . Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate both their professional knowledge and their ability to communicate effectively in English. Stage Three: Final Fellowship Selection Following the interviews, the final group of fellows will be selected. Successful applicants will need to sign a learning contract to complete the admission process. The final selection therefore considers more than academic qualifications alone and incorporates performance during the programme s assessment and interview stages. Fellowship Funding and Financial Support The FOR-GHP Fellowship has no tuition fees . The fellowship budget provides financial support for participation in the three mandatory in-person workshops. Covered expenses include: Economy-class flights Visa fees Accommodation Daily meals during the workshops However, participants will not receive daily allowances or per diems . Applicants should therefore understand the distinction between the expenses covered by the programme and personal expenses that may not be covered. Important Visa Information Because the first workshop is scheduled to take place in Hamburg, Germany , selected participants will need to arrange the appropriate visa where required. Applicants are strongly encouraged to consider booking a German embassy visa appointment in December 2026 , even before receiving the final fellowship outcome, because visa appointment and processing times can be lengthy. This recommendation is particularly relevant for applicants who require a visa to enter Germany. Applicants should independently confirm the applicable visa requirements and procedures for their nationality and place of residence. Gender Inclusion The FOR-GHP programme encourages applications from people of all gender identities . The programme seeks to build a diverse network of public health professionals working to strengthen outbreak preparedness and response across sub-Saharan Africa. How to Apply for the FOR-GHP Fellowship Interested applicants must complete the online application form and submit all required supporting documentation. The application package should include the required eligibility and supporting documents, including a motivation letter in English in PDF format . Applicants should ensure that every required document is completed and submitted before the deadline. The programme states that: Applications must be submitted electronically. Hard-copy applications will not be accepted. Applications should not be sent by email. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Applicants should submit the required documentation through the official online application system. FOR-GHP Fellowship Application Deadline The application deadline is: 21 October 2026 at midnight CET Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly because incomplete applications will not be considered. Application Link Applicants can access the official online application form through the FOR-GHP application portal. APPLY HERE Who Should Apply for the FOR-GHP Fellowship? The fellowship is particularly relevant to professionals who are already working in public health or biomedical environments and want to strengthen their expertise in outbreak readiness and become trainers and multipliers within their institutions. Potentially suitable applicants include professionals working in areas such as: Public health Epidemiology Medicine Microbiology Biology Infectious disease prevention and control Public health surveillance Health emergency preparedness Biomedical sciences Allied health sciences Public health training and capacity development Applicants should have at least two years of relevant professional experience , be connected to the sub-Saharan African region , have appropriate academic or professional qualifications, and have the support of their current employer. Visit HERE to learn more about the FOR-GHP Fellowship 2027–2028. Key Dates for the FOR-GHP Fellowship Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Activity Date Fellowship applications close 21 October 2026, midnight CET Seven eLearning modules 1 December 2026 – 1 January 2027 First workshop, Hamburg 12–17 April 2027 Second workshop, Accra 11–15 October 2027 Third workshop, Kampala 3–7 July 2028 Expected programme duration Approximately 1.5 years What Makes the FOR-GHP Fellowship Different? The fellowship combines professional development with institutional and regional capacity strengthening. Instead of focusing exclusively on classroom-based learning, the programme requires fellows to apply their knowledge by developing and implementing teaching case studies in their own institutions. The Training-of-Trainers model means participants are expected to become knowledge multipliers. This can allow the impact of the programme to extend beyond the individual fellow to colleagues, institutions, professional networks, and public health systems. The combination of: eLearning Face-to-face workshops Simulation exercises Case-study development Teaching practice Institutional implementation Leadership development Regional networking Peer learning Mentorship provides a comprehensive approach to professional development in outbreak readiness. Tips for Applicants Applicants can strengthen the quality of their application by carefully demonstrating how their professional experience aligns with the goals of the fellowship. Particular attention should be given to the following: Demonstrate relevant professional experience Clearly explain your experience in public health, biomedical work, infectious disease prevention, surveillance, preparedness, or response. Show institutional relevance Explain how the skills gained through FOR-GHP could contribute to your current institution and public health work. Highlight training or mentorship experience Because the programme follows a multiplier and Training-of-Trainers model, applicants should clearly demonstrate any experience they have in training, mentoring, facilitating workshops, sharing knowledge, or developing educational materials. Prepare the employer endorsement early The employer endorsement is an important requirement because the fellowship involves three international workshops and implementation of a teaching case study at the applicant s institution. Applicants should therefore engage their employers early rather than waiting until the application deadline. Prepare for online learning The first seven eLearning modules are part of the selection process. Applicants should ensure that they have access to a suitable computer, reliable internet, and the necessary audio and microphone equipment. Prepare for English-language interviews Applicants who progress to the interview stage should be ready for an individual interview conducted in English via Zoom. Begin considering visa arrangements Applicants who require a German visa should pay attention to the programme s recommendation regarding early visa appointments, particularly because the first workshop is scheduled to take place in Hamburg in April 2027. Conclusion The FOR-GHP Fellowship in Outbreak Readiness for Global Health Protection provides an extensive professional development opportunity for public health and biomedical professionals working in sub-Saharan Africa. Through its blended Training-of-Trainers approach, the programme addresses several areas that are central to modern outbreak preparedness, including infectious disease surveillance, public health intelligence, One Health, emergency preparedness, communication, leadership, systems thinking, training, mentorship, and regional collaboration. The fellowship also goes beyond individual learning by requiring participants to develop and implement teaching case studies within their home institutions. This multiplier approach is intended to help translate fellowship learning into broader institutional and regional capacity. There are no tuition fees , while the programme provides support for economy-class travel, visa fees, accommodation, and meals associated with the three in-person workshops in Hamburg, Accra, and Kampala. Qualified professionals from sub-Saharan Africa with at least two years of public health or biomedical experience and relevant academic or professional backgrounds are encouraged to consider applying. title: EGD Grant Program for Peace & Value Education: Funding for Community-Led Peace, Values and Social Impact Projects

The EGD Grant Program provides an opportunity for people with community-focused ideas to seek funding for projects that contribute to stronger relationships, mutual understanding, peaceful engagement, and values-based education within their communities. At the heart of the program is an emphasis on people-led and community-based action . Rather than limiting participation to established organisations or a particular age group, the program invites individuals and groups to present project ideas that can contribute meaningfully to peace and value education at the community level. Youth-led initiatives are particularly encouraged to apply. However, the opportunity is open to applicants of all ages , allowing a broad range of community members, educators, young people, and other individuals interested in peace and values education to submit their ideas for consideration. About Educational Globale et Développement (EGD) The Educational Globale et Développement Grant Program for Peace Value Education focuses on supporting initiatives that promote peace, cooperation, mutual understanding, universal human values, and community learning. Through the grant application process, EGD is seeking people-led and community-based initiatives capable of creating positive social impact. What Is the EGD Grant Program for Peace Value Education? The EGD Grant Program for Peace Value Education is a funding opportunity for projects that contribute to peace and human universal values through community-level initiatives. The application process is designed to collect information from prospective applicants and understand: The project or initiative they are proposing; The intended outcomes of the project; How the initiative contributes to peace and value education; How the project relates to the applicant s community; The potential for the initiative to encourage dialogue and mutual understanding; How the proposed activities can contribute to cooperation and community learning; and The positive social impact the applicant hopes to achieve. EGD is interested in people-led and community-based initiatives that promote peace, universal human values, cooperation, dialogue, mutual understanding, community learning, and positive social impact. Projects may seek to create opportunities for people to communicate, exchange ideas, learn from one another, and better understand different experiences and perspectives. Applicants proposing dialogue-based activities should explain what they hope participants will learn or achieve through these interactions. 4. Mutual Understanding The program seeks initiatives capable of strengthening mutual understanding. Projects can therefore consider how education and community participation can help individuals better understand one another and contribute to stronger community relationships. 5. Cooperation EGD also highlights cooperation as an important component of the program. Applicants can demonstrate how their project will encourage participants, groups, educators, community members, or other stakeholders to work together toward positive outcomes. 6. Community Learning Projects that facilitate learning at the community level can also align with the objectives of the grant. Applicants should consider how participants will gain knowledge, skills, awareness, understanding, or values through the proposed activities. 7. Importantly, youth-led programs are encouraged . However, the program is not restricted exclusively to young people. EGD explicitly states that all ages are welcome to apply . This makes the grant accessible to a broad range of people interested in designing and implementing initiatives that support peace and values education. Strong Encouragement for Youth-Led Initiatives One notable aspect of the EGD Grant Program is its encouragement of youth-led programming. Why Community-Based Initiatives Matter to the Program The EGD Grant Program specifically highlights people-led and community-based initiatives . This means applicants should pay close attention to the relationship between their proposed activities and the community they intend to serve. A strong project description should clearly establish: The community context: Explain where or within what community the project will operate. The issue or opportunity: Identify what the project seeks to address or improve. The proposed activities: Explain what will actually happen through the project. The participants or beneficiaries: Describe the people the initiative intends to engage or benefit. The connection to peace and values: Demonstrate how the project advances peace, universal human values, cooperation, dialogue, mutual understanding, or community learning. Applicants should therefore think carefully about several questions before submitting their application. What is your project idea? Clearly explain the initiative you want to implement. Avoid relying solely on broad statements about promoting peace. Instead, explain what activities you plan to carry out and how they will work. Why is the project needed? Consider the circumstances within your community that make the proposed initiative relevant. The connection between the identified need and the proposed activities should be easy for reviewers to understand. Who will participate? Identify the community members, young people, educators, groups, or other participants the project intends to involve. What will the project achieve? The intended outcomes should be clearly stated. Applicants should explain what they hope will change, improve, or develop as a result of the initiative. How does the project promote peace and values? This is particularly important because peace and value education are central to the funding opportunity. Applicants should directly explain how their activities will advance these objectives. What positive social impact could result? Consider both immediate and broader outcomes. For example, applicants can explain how participants may benefit from increased learning, dialogue, understanding, cooperation, or stronger community relationships where these outcomes are relevant to their proposed initiative. How to Develop a Strong Project Proposal Applicants should ensure that their proposal is clear, practical, community-focused, and closely connected to the objectives of the EGD Grant Program. When preparing an application, consider the following approach: Step 1: Identify a clear community need Start by identifying the issue, challenge, or opportunity the project will address. Step 2: Define the project objective Explain what the initiative is intended to accomplish. Applicants should make it possible for reviewers to understand how the proposed project would move from an idea to practical implementation. Step 4: Identify the intended participants Explain who will participate in or benefit from the initiative. This could include youth, community members, learners, educators, or other relevant groups depending on the nature of the proposed project. Step 5: Describe the expected outcomes Applicants should identify what they expect the project to achieve. Where possible, outcomes should be specific enough for reviewers to understand what successful implementation would look like. Step 6: Connect the project directly to EGD s objectives Applicants should clearly establish the relationship between their proposal and the broader goals of peace and value education. A project may have several positive community benefits, but the application should specifically demonstrate why it belongs within this particular grant program.
